newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former Filipina sex slaves demand compensation.
newsitem.headline: Former Filipina sex slaves demand compensation.

text.p: Dozens of Filipinas used as World War Two sex slaves pressed their demand for compensation from Japan on Thursday at a rally which coincided with a Southeast Asia tour by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

One of the "comfort women," now greying, sickly grandmothers, collapsed during the one-hour picket outside the Japanese embassy in Manila's Makati financial district. Her colleagues said she was suffering from cancer of the ovaries.
"We hope our appeals will reach Japan. We are dying one by one. How come they still don't want to give us justice?" Dolores Molina, 67, said between sobs during a speech during the rally.
Molina said she was 14 when Japanese soldiers imprisoned her in a garrison for a month where she was repeatedly raped.

More than 40 women took part in the protest, which took place as Hashimoto arrived in Indonesia on the third leg of a five-nation tour of member countries of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
He has visited Brunei and Malaysia and will be travelling to Singapore and Vietnam. He toured two other ASEAN members, Thailand and the Philippines, last year.
The protesters were among 169 Filipinas, aged 66 to 85, whom a Manila human rights group has identified as among local women Japanese soldiers forced into battlefront brothels.
Eight women last year each accepted "atonement money" of $18,500 from the private Asian Women's Fund set up in Japan. The payment was accompanied by a letter of apology from Hashimoto.

But many others refused to accept the reparation, saying the money should come from the government to show Japan's official admission of its responsibility. They are each demanding state reparation of $200,000.
Seventeen of the women have died, the latest of a heart attack on Tuesday.
Nelia Sancho, the leader of a group which helped organise the rally, said the protest was "to highlight the urgency" for action by Tokyo.
"We hope in his (Hashimoto's) tour he will know the sentiments of the people, specially the women victims of the war," she said.
